sources.note: BASS one-page document: observations of burning solid materials on board the ISS

objective.value: Examine the burning and extinction characteristics of a wide variety of solid fuel samples in microgravity, to guide strategies for extinguishing accidental fires in microgravity and to feed combustion models used in the design of fire detection and suppression systems in space and on Earth.

sources.note: BASS document states the investigation examines burning and extinction of a wide variety of fuel samples in microgravity to guide fire-extinguishing strategies
BASS document: guides strategies for extinguishing fires (suppression) and links results to NASA-STD-6001 material selection and radiative heat release (prevention)
Challenge brief, 'Background': flammability studies of solids such as fabrics and plastics feed prevention / material selection

safety_functions.note: Suppression is stated directly; prevention follows from the material-selection framing.

sources.note: BASS document: observations of burning solid materials and a wide variety of solid fuel samples
BASS document lists SIBAL cotton-fiberglass fabric, Nomex, Ultem, PMMA (thick flats and spheres), wax-saturated fiberglass, and paraffin and Japan wax candle fuels

fuel_geometry.value: Three sample classes: thin flat sheets (about 12 cm x 1-2 cm), thick flat slabs (5 cm x 1 cm x 1-2 mm), and solid PMMA spheres (1 and 2 cm diameter); plus candles in a thin ceramic tube (6 mm diameter x 25 mm long).

sources.note: BASS document gives the sample categories and dimensions (thin flats, thick flats, PMMA spheres, ceramic-tube candles)
BASS document: hardware sits within the MSG on board the ISS

apparatus.value: Slightly modified Smoke Point In Co-flow Experiment (SPICE) hardware: a small flow duct with an igniter and a nitrogen nozzle, and a fan that produces a co-flow of air across the sample.

sources.note: BASS document: slightly modified SPICE hardware, a small flow duct with igniter and small nozzle; a fan produces co-flow through the duct

o2_percent.note: No readable source states an oxygen range for BASS (I). The BASS one-page PDF gives no oxygen concentration. Left unknown; a combined BASS/BASS-II figure that exists is noted in review.notes.

pressure_psi.note: No readable source states a pressure range for BASS (I). The BASS one-page PDF gives no pressure. Left unknown rather than inferred.

sources.note: BASS document: the crewmember adjusts the airflow from 5 to 50 cm/s through the duct; airflow direction along the sample is concurrent or opposed

airflow.note: PDF gives a crew-adjustable 5-50 cm/s; NASA/NTRS papers instead cite wind-tunnel speeds up to 40 cm/s, so confidence is medium (see review.notes).

sources.note: BASS document frames the tests as microgravity burning aboard the ISS; the exact g level is not stated
Challenge brief: low-gravity combustion experiments conducted on the ISS

gravity_g.note: ISS platform treated as microgravity (~0 g).

sources.note: BASS document: nitrogen is supplied as a flame suppressant (0 to 500 cc/min) through a mass flow controller; the PDF calls it a suppressant rather than a chamber diluent

diluents.note: Nitrogen is used in BASS largely as the injected suppressant; glovebox working-volume nitrogen vitiation is explicitly described for BASS-II, not for BASS-I, hence low confidence.

value: Fuel type, thickness and geometry (thin and thick flats, PMMA spheres, wax candles)
Nitrogen suppressant flow rate (0 to 500 cc/min)
Ignition location (front or back of the PMMA spheres)

sources.note: BASS document: tests vary fuel samples/geometry, tunnel flow speed, nitrogen flow rate and ignition location
BASS paper: effects of air flow speed, fuel thickness, fuel preheating and nitrogen dilution in opposed and concurrent flow

held_constant.note: Sources describe varied flow, fuel and suppression but do not enumerate which conditions were held constant across BASS-I tests.

sources.note: BASS document: an anemometer measures the actual flow rate and a radiometer measures flame output; video and still cameras record each test

relevance_notes.value: Named in the challenge brief as a solid-material flammability study for prevention / material selection, and the experiment directly tests burning and extinction of solids in microgravity to guide fire-extinguishing strategies for crewed spacecraft.

sources.note: Challenge brief, 'Background': flammability studies focus on solid materials such as fabrics and plastics (BASS and BASS-II)
BASS document: will guide strategies for extinguishing accidental fires in microgravity

value: Combustion models validated in the simpler microgravity flow environment are used to build more complex models for flames burning in normal gravity
Applies to the general understanding of many terrestrial combustion problems and ground-based microgravity combustion research

sources.note: BASS document 'Earth Applications': validated models have wide applicability to the general understanding of many terrestrial combustion problems
